title: Composite-Fermion Study of Cavity-Modified Fractional Quantum Hall Excitation Gaps
authors: Dalin Boriçi, Nicolas Regnault, Cristiano Ciuti
abstract: We investigate how cavity-mediated attractive electron-electron interactions modify the excitation gaps of fractional quantum Hall states within the composite-fermion framework. We compute both the neutral magnetoroton excitation spectrum and the charged excitation gap relevant to transport experiments for the Laughlin $ν=1/3$ and $ν=1/5$ states. We consider a spin-polarized lowest-Landau-level model in which the interaction is mediated by a cavity mode with a spatially uniform vacuum-field gradient and a finite interaction range controlled by a long-distance cutoff. Finite-size scaling reveals that the transport gap is consistently enhanced by the cavity-induced interaction, with the gap enhancement scaling quadratically with the electron number and with the fourth power of the vacuum-field gradient. By contrast, the magnetoroton spectrum exhibits a richer dependence on the interaction range. The high-$k$ magnetoroton gap is enhanced for all interaction ranges considered, consistent with its close connection to the charged excitation gap, even with the long-range character of the interaction.
summary:
This paper theoretically examines the effect of attractive, cavity-mediated interactions on the excitation gaps of Fractional Quantum Hall liquids. Using the composite-fermion framework, the authors calculate both neutral and charged gap shifts for $
u=1/3$ and $
u=1/5$. The key finding is a robust enhancement of the transport gap that scales predictably with system size and cavity field strength.
main_problem: The study investigates how attractive electron-electron interactions mediated by a cavity modify the excitation gaps of Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) states.
main_result: Finite-size scaling analysis shows that the transport gap is enhanced quadratically with the electron number and the fourth power of the vacuum-field gradient. The high-$k$ magnetoroton gap also exhibits enhancement.
method: The calculations utilize the composite-fermion (CF) framework, analyzing both neutral magnetoroton spectra and charged excitation gaps relevant to transport experiments.
model_or_system:
The system is a spin-polarized lowest-Landau-level model of FQH liquids ($
u=1/3, 1/5$) coupled to a single quantized cavity mode. The effective interaction potential modifies the Coulomb pseudopotentials.
key_observables: Neutral magnetoroton excitation spectrum and charged excitation gap (relevant to transport).
important_parameters:
Filling factors ($
u=1/3, 1/5$), electron number ($N$), cavity vacuum-field gradient ($G$), and interaction range parameter ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a spatially uniform cavity-field gradient; the CF framework is used as an approximation for the strongly interacting system.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate quadratic scaling of the charge gap with $N$ (Fig. 1, 9), confirm the dependence on interaction range ($L/\sqrt{S}$) (Fig. 2, 11), and show thermodynamic extrapolation confirming finite limits for the gap shift (Fig. 3, 10).
paper_structure: The paper develops the effective Hamiltonian using CF theory, calculates expectation values of the cavity interaction, analyzes both neutral and charged excitation gaps, and employs finite-size scaling to extrapolate results to the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges concepts from cavity QED (cavity coupling) into strongly correlated electron physics (FQH states), providing a quantitative prediction for how external electromagnetic environments can tune fundamental many-body properties like excitation gaps.
